versions.localizedDescription: Mirrored from [Apollo-Reborn v1.15.11_4.0.1](https://github.com/Apollo-Reborn/Apollo-Reborn/releases/tag/v1.15.11_4.0.1). These IPAs are the **official Apollo-Reborn builds**, re-hosted here so this long-standing AltStore source keeps working for existing users. Apollo-Reborn also runs its own website and sources at https://apolloreborn.app --- ### Performance - Send fewer Reddit requests on **API-Key-Free** accounts by not repeating link preview lookups for sites that block previews and by briefly reusing the Inbox's reply lookups, so ordinary reading reaches Reddit's rate limit later (#1579: @icpryde) - New replies, and anything you post or edit, still refresh right away ### Fixes - Fix **multi-photo posts** showing a reddit.com link and 0 photos since Reddit began marking their photos as failed, so the gallery, feed carousel, media viewer, Save All and Gallery View show them again (#1589: @icpryde) - Covers galleries posted from Apollo with Reddit as the Media Upload Host and from other apps; they show as square cards in the feed - Fix **API-Key-Free search** showing "Error searching" or "Error loading subreddits" for post search, searching within a subreddit or multireddit, and subreddit search (#1557: @DeltAndy123) - Fix **All Posts (r/all)** showing "Couldn't load posts" on **API-Key-Free** accounts, for every sort and with Exclude Subscriptions (#1570: @icpryde) - All Posts has another way in before Old Reddit, and if Reddit blocks another **API-Key-Free** read, a route update can work around it without an app update (#1594: @DeltAndy123) - Open the feed you chose to start on again at launch by turning **Restore Reading Session** off by default; # Changelog ## 1.0.0 (build 3) First release. - SEGA Superstars Tennis (Xbox 360) on iPhone and iPad, recompiled with the iOS port of ReXGlue and drawn through Vulkan on Metal (MoltenVK). iOS 15 or later. - Direct Xbox 360 ISO/XISO loading with **Choose ISO**, or extracted disc files in the app's `game` folder. - Matches at up to 60 FPS, capped at 60. CPU readback of the shaders' memory exports is off by default: it made the GPU thread wait for the GPU 30-50 times a frame (12-14 FPS in a match on an iPhone 14 Pro Max). - The game's busy waits (Direct3D's wait for the GPU, the audio threads' barrier) sleep briefly instead of spinning a core, which keeps the phone cooler during long sessions. - The picture stays landscape and sharp after Notification Center, Control Center, screenshots and app switches. iOS lays the window out in portrait for its background snapshot, and the swap chain used to stay portrait afterwards. - On-screen touch controls when no controller is connected; MFi, Xbox and PlayStation controllers. - Pause and resume on app switches and locking; game language from the device; shader and pipeline caches kept across launches; Apple Game Mode.

KartPad 0.8.6 (build 268) fixes PadMint builds, which had stopped for everyone after an upstream change, gives the game your country for the online flag and globe, adds two speed options for slower Android phones and custom GPU drivers for Snapdragon phones, brings in WiiCompiled's fixes through v0.9.0, makes the Android game code faster, and lets Android players try WiiCompiled 0.9's new graphics engine. Retro Rewind stays at 6.13.4. ### New - **Your country online:** Mario Kart Wii reads your country from the Wii's system settings, and KartPad never provided it, so online matchmaking showed no flag and put your Mii in the wrong place on the globe. KartPad now gives the game a country, the same way a Wii does: your device's region, or on Android one you choose. On Android, change it in **⋯ → Multiplayer → Country…**. Your Mii goes on the globe at your country's capital. Existing saves load as before, with no "create new save data" prompt, in Original and Retro Rewind ([#511](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/511)). - **30 FPS Races (Android):** **⋯ → Graphics & Performance → 30 FPS Races** switches single-player races to the game's own 30 FPS mode, the one it uses for 3 and 4 players. The race runs at normal speed while the game draws half as often, so a phone that slows down at 60 FPS can play at full speed. Time Trials and ghost races stay at 60 FPS. Off by default ([#339](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/339), [#510](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/510)). - **Simpler Computer Karts (Android):** **⋯ → Graphics & Performance → Simpler Computer Karts** gives computer karts the simpler models the game uses in split-screen. They look less detailed and their drivers don't animate; your kart, ghosts and online players are unchanged. Off by default. Thanks to [DriftDroid](https://github.com/dorPXP/driftdroid), where this idea comes from. - **Custom GPU drivers (Android, Snapdragon):** **⋯ → Graphics & Performance → GPU Driver** installs a driver package (the AdrenoTools `.zip` format other Android emulators use, such as Turnip) and uses it with either graphics engine. Many Adreno graphics faults are driver bugs, and a newer driver is the only fix for those. If a driver doesn't load, or graphics can't start with it, or the game closes twice while starting, KartPad goes back to the phone's own driver by itself. Problem reports say which driver was running. - **Choose your graphics engine on Android (beta):** WiiCompiled 0.9 replaced its graphics layer with a newer one. KartPad 0.8.6 for Android ships both. **Classic** is the default and keeps every KartPad graphics fix, including the Adreno character and track workarounds. **WiiCompiled 0.9 (Beta)** uses the new renderer. Switch in **⋯ → Graphics & Performance → Graphics Engine** or with **Graphics** on the KartPad start screen; the game restarts, and your saves, settings and controller assignments stay. If anything looks wrong, switch back to Classic; if the beta closes twice while starting, KartPad goes back to Classic by itself. The beta starts with shaders recorded on the menus and seven Mushroom and Flower Cup courses, and prepares every shader it has seen at launch, so other courses may pause briefly only the first time you visit them. The first time it starts after installing or updating, the beta prepares these shaders behind a "Compiling shaders" screen; on a Pixel 9 Pro XL that took about 20 seconds. Each engine keeps its own shaders, so switching engines doesn't make either one compile them again. Of KartPad's Adreno workarounds, the beta has only the native uniform buffers option in **Android Graphics Diagnostics…**; the vertex and matrix workarounds are Classic only. Phones with a Qualcomm Adreno GPU get a warning before trying it. On Android the beta now asks the display for the game's frame rate, as Classic does, and if Vulkan isn't available it stops with a clear message instead of starting without graphics. Problem rep

KartPad 0.8.5 (build 267) updates Retro Rewind to 6.13.4 and adds the requested rumble-strength and stick-click controls on Android, plus a quicker touch item hold on Android and iPhone/iPad. ### Added - **Android rumble strength:** in **Controls → Controller Button Mapping…**, adjust **Rumble strength** from 0% to 200%. 100% is the standard setting; lower it for gentler feedback or raise it for stronger feedback. It applies to controller motors and the device-vibration fallback for handheld controls. The existing **Rumble** switch still turns both off. Devices without amplitude control may not change physical strength. - **L3 and R3 mappings on Android:** either stick click is now a mapping option. Map **D-pad Up — Trick / Wheelie** to L3 or R3 to trick without reaching for the D-pad. Existing mappings stay the same until you change them. ### Changed - **Retro Rewind 6.13.4:** updated the official pack, code hashes and compiled game code together. Install the matching content through **Download / Update Retro Rewind…** after updating KartPad. Existing saves, ghosts and imported soundtrack files are preserved by the update path. - **Quicker touch item hold:** with the optional setting enabled, hold touch L for 0.67 seconds instead of one second to keep the item held behind your kart. Tap L again to let go. This applies to Android and iPhone/iPad; touch auto-accelerate still uses one second ([#473](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/473)). ### Updating - **Android:** **Update available → Update Now**, or install the APK over your current KartPad. Don't uninstall first. Then update Retro Rewind to 6.13.4 in KartPad. - **iPhone and iPad:** build 0.8.5 with the latest [PadMint](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/padmint/releases/latest) and install over your current KartPad with the same sideloading tool and Apple ID. Then update Retro Rewind in KartPad. The `ios-for-padmint.ipa` is an input for PadMint and does not contain game code. - **Apple Silicon Mac:** rebuild through PadMint, choose **Mario Kart Wii → This Mac**, and select the matching 6.13.4 Retro Rewind data produced by that build. Your saves stay. ### Validation scope Gameplay, emulator and physical-device testing were skipped at the owner's request. This release does not claim a graphics or performance fix. Existing missing-character reports remain open. Android and iOS compiled from the clean release commit. The Android APK passed both package audits, two independent signed derivations were byte-identical, and its signing identity matches 0.8.4. The iOS PadMint input passed the final package audit and contains no game code. The compiled Android package contains the new control UI and matching Retro Rewind 6.13.4 pack. The source archive includes reviewed translator marker strings and synthetic test fixtures. The Android-only translated-code findings are the documented KartPad release exception; no private game inputs or signing material are packaged. Mac: the required clean PadMint player build passed before tagging, using Apple Python 3.9 and an empty PadMint folder. Its 0.8.5/build 267 app passed deep signature verification.

KartPad 0.8.4 (build 266) adds rumble on Android, Retro Rewind soundtrack packs, an optional touch item hold and a new test for invisible characters on Snapdragon phones. iPhone and iPad copies that still need their PadMint build now say so, and PadMint builds ride out dropped downloads. ### Added - **Rumble on Android:** rumble never worked on Android. Controllers with their own motor now rumble. When player one's controller has no motor, such as a handheld's built-in controls, the device itself vibrates, as in Dolphin. A **Rumble** switch in **Controls → Controller Button Mapping…** is on by default and turns both off. Touch-only play doesn't vibrate ([#497](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/497)). - **Retro Rewind soundtrack packs:** add `.brstm` files, or a soundtrack pack's `.zip`, in **Game Data & Saves → Retro Rewind Music…** on Android and iPhone/iPad. A file named like one of Retro Rewind's tracks (for example `104_N.brstm`, and `104_F.brstm` for the final lap) replaces it the next time KartPad starts, and your music stays when Retro Rewind updates. On a Mac, put the files in the `MyStuff` folder of the `RetroRewind6` folder you chose ([#441](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/441), [#499](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/499)). - **Touch item hold** (Android and iPhone/iPad, off by default): in **Controls → Touch Control Settings**. Holding touch L for one second keeps your item held behind the kart, so you can steer and drift while trailing a shell or banana. Press L again to let go ([#473](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/473), [#500](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/500)). - **Android graphics:** **Help → Character Graphics Test → Experimental: bone index per vertex** is a new attempt for Snapdragon phones where riders are invisible or only their heads show. It hasn't been tried on an affected phone yet, so a log with it on helps ([#104](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/issues/104), [#498](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/498)). ### Changed - **iPhone and iPad:** the `ios-for-padmint.ipa` on the releases page has no game code; PadMint adds it. Installed by itself, or over an older KartPad that already had game data, it used to say **Ready to play** and then stop at a PadMint message that only mentioned a Mac. Now the game cards say **Needs your PadMint build**, the message explains that PadMint runs on a Mac, Windows or Linux computer and that saves and imported game data stay, and **Help → Getting Started** starts with the PadMint step ([#494](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/494)). Copies built with PadMint are unchanged. - **PadMint builds:** a dropped or stalled download (the Retro Rewind pack, the Retro-WFC payload, Dawn or `sse2neon.h`) is tried again up to three times instead of stopping the build with "Remote end closed connection without response". If it still fails, the message names the server and says it's a network problem ([#495](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/495)). - **PadMint recipe:** iPhone, iPad and Android builds ask for 16 GB free instead of 60 GB, the measured need ([#490](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/kartpad/pull/490)). Retro Rewind stays at 6.13.3. ### Updating - **Android:** **Update available → Update Now**, or install the APK over your current KartPad. Saves, licenses, ghosts and game data stay. - **iPhone, iPad and Mac:** build 0.8.4 with the latest [PadMint](https://github.com/chrissotraidis/padmint/releases/latest) and install it over your current KartPad with the same sideloading tool and Apple ID. Saves and game data stay.

versions.localizedDescription: ## New - **The Google Photos app now counts what this app backs up.** ([#24](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/pull/24), thanks @saileshbro) Uploads showed as "not backed up" in the Google Photos app, and its own **Free up space** never offered them. It now recognises them, and its **Free up space** and **Delete from device** remove the photos from your iPhone. On one library of about 8,500 items, "Not backed up" went from 8,145 to 0 and **Free up space** from 2 items to 461. The reason was the version being uploaded. The Google Photos app only counts a photo it can match to the one on your iPhone, so an **edited** photo or video now backs up as it looks, not as its unedited original. A photo you edited in the Google Photos app also needs the version that edit was applied on, which is uploaded in an extra step. - **Back Up Live Photo Motion.** Off by default. With it on, a Live Photo's motion is attached to the still already in your account, so it plays as a Live Photo and **Free up space** will offer it. Live Photos backed up earlier get their motion added as a backlog — this can be tens of GB, which is why it is a setting you turn on. - **Backup keeps going after you leave the app (iOS 26).** While the app is open with work to do, iOS is asked to keep it running; progress then shows in a Live Activity, where you can also stop it. Up to 2 uploads run at once in the background. On earlier iOS versions nothing changes. ## Fixed - **Automatic Backup never ran in the background on SideStore installs.** This affected every sideloaded install and was not new in this release. SideStore renames the app when it signs it, so the background task the app registered no longer matched the one it declared, and iOS refused it — meaning **Automatic Backup never got a background window at all**. The app now reads the name from its own build. ([#2](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/2)) - **Google's rate limit no longer fails a row.** When Google asked the app to slow down (HTTP 429), rows retried a second apart, met the same refusal, and failed. The whole queue now waits it out — a minute, doubling up to ten while Google keeps refusing — and carries on. - **Items marked "Cancelled" with no reason.** ([#19](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/19)) If the app was interrupted part way through an item, that row was marked "Cancelled" and left with nothing to explain it and nothing to retry it, which is why the same photo could appear as both "Cancelled" and "Already backed up". An interruption now retries, and if it keeps happening it says what went wrong. "Cancelled" now only ever means you stopped it, and reads **Stopped by you**. - **The activity list got faster on big backups.** ([#8](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/8)) As each item finished, the app was asking the photo library about it twice on the same thread that draws the list. It asks once now. - **Photos deleted while still queued.** Freeing space on your iPhone deletes photos that may still be waiting to upload. Those rows are dropped quietly instead of failing with "no longer in your photo library" — about 2,000 rows had failed that way on one library. - **Hand-picked photos are re-checked** even when the app already remembers them as backed up. ## Verifying this release - **The `.ipa` is built by GitHub Actions from the tagged commit**, not on a laptop, and is attached with its SHA-256 as `PhotosBackup.ipa.sha256`. ([#17](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/pull/17), thanks @nonnapopoa, raised in [#15](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/15)) You can check the file you downloaded with `shasum -a 256 PhotosBackup.ipa` and compare, and the build log shows which commit and toolchain produced it. - Every pull request and every push now runs the test suite before it can land. ## Worth knowing - **An edited photo now backs up its edit, not its original.** Originals already uploaded stay in your account, but a newly edited photo no longer uploa

## New - **Back Up Photos in Shortcuts (iOS 16+).** ([#7](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/7)) Add it to a personal automation — when the iPhone connects to power, at a time of day, or when it joins your home Wi-Fi — and set it to run immediately. Each run finds new photos in your selected albums and hands them to iOS to upload in the background. It works with **Automatic Backup** off, so a schedule of your own can replace it ([#14](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/14)), and it still follows **Use Connection** and **Pause**. **Settings → Shortcuts** shows when it last ran and what it did. iOS gives each run about 30 seconds, so the action spends them finding and preparing photos, then leaves the uploads to iOS. With the app open it just adds to the queue — the uploads you are watching are not interrupted. Photos stored only in iCloud still wait until you open the app. - **Diagnostic reports you can attach to an issue.** **Settings → Support → Create Diagnostic Report** builds a text file you can share or copy. It opens with **What stands out** — the likely reason backup is not happening, in plain words (Background App Refresh off, Low Power Mode, a paused or stopped queue, no background window from iOS in days, too little free space, and more). Below that: your settings, the last 40 runs, crash and termination data from iOS, the upload queue, and a timeline of what the app did and why. It leaves out credentials, account addresses, photo identifiers, filenames, media, and links, so it is safe to post publicly. - **See when iOS actually runs the backup.** **Settings → Support → Diagnostics → Recent Runs** lists every run — opening the app, **Back Up Now**, Shortcuts, and the background windows iOS grants — with the time it started, how long it took, what it did, and the conditions it ran under (network, battery and charging, Low Power Mode, locked or not). Background windows also record how long after the request iOS started them. - **Event Timeline.** Every decision the app makes now leaves an entry saying why: why a background run was or wasn't requested, why uploads paused, which step an upload failed at and what Google said, when an item waited for iCloud, what iOS delivered while the app was closed. It keeps two weeks of history; repeats fold into one line, and warnings and errors are kept longer than routine entries, so a big backup does not push out the one failure that matters. - **Storage.** **Settings → Support → Storage** shows what the app keeps on your phone — pending upload copies, backup history, transfer receipts, caches — and **Clean Up Unused Data** removes leftovers without touching pending uploads or your account. ## Fixed - **One photo can no longer make the app close on every launch.** ([#13](https://github.com/g8row/PhotosBackup/issues/13)) If the app stopped while preparing a photo or video, the next launch started with that same item, so a single file that took the app down meant it closed again every time you opened it and nothing else backed up. Now an item the app stopped on goes to the end of the queue, and if it stops the app a second time it is skipped with an explanation — tap it to retry. Everything else keeps backing up. Suspending the app normally never counts against an item, so iOS closing the app in the background does not skip anything. - **Checking a large video uses less memory.** The file is read in pieces, and each piece is now released as soon as it has been checked, instead of possibly being held until the whole video is done. - **The app knows when it last closed unexpectedly.** If it disappears while open, while starting, or during a background run, the next launch records it and the report says so — even when iOS did not share a crash report. - **Leftover transfer receipts are cleaned up.** Receipts that no upload owns any more are removed a day after they were written, and Google's responses are no longer kept in a disk cache. ## Explained - **"Storage save

## Fixed - **"Google returned HTTP 400" during finalization now recovers instead of failing the photo.** A live run against Google reproduced it: an upload whose receipt comes back without its upload token is committed anyway, Google answers *"At least one valid blueprint is required"*, and every retry replayed the same dead receipt. The receipt is now checked where it is produced and where it is used, and a rejected one costs the item one fresh transfer rather than its whole retry budget. Receipts saved by older versions are checked too, so a queue carrying one from before the update recovers on the next attempt. - **A full Google account stops the backup and says so.** It used to arrive as a generic HTTP failure, so the queue kept going and failed every remaining photo the same way, one at a time. Backup now pauses with an explanation and waits — freeing space and tapping **Resume** picks it back up. It does not ask you to reconnect the account, because signing in again does not free storage. - **Every upload commits under the quality setting you have selected now.** The choice between original quality and Storage Saver, and whether the upload counts against your Google storage, was captured when the photo was prepared and then kept with it — so a photo prepared while Storage Saver was on kept uploading as Storage Saver after you turned it off, including after restarting the app. ## Improved - **A failed upload will tell you what Google said.** Tap a failed row for the full reason, selectable, with **Copy Details**. **Diagnostics** keeps the last 25 failures with their error codes and a **Copy All**, and counts how many there have been — the reason used to be a two-line caption that disappeared as soon as the row was retried or cleared. - **Error messages name what failed.** "Google returned HTTP 400 during finalization" rather than "check your connection", and Google's own explanation is decoded instead of shown as a hex dump. - **A long backup no longer slows down as it progresses.** The activity list, navigation, and the uploads themselves got slower the further into a whole-library backup you were: the queue's counters, its row lookups, and its search for the next upload all walked the entire queue on every progress update, and the per-album "backed up" counts re-scanned every selected album on each of those too. All of it is now maintained as it goes, so the cost no longer grows with the size of the queue. ## Notes - 132 tests, 130 passing (2 opt-in live tests skipped). - Verified against Google with a fresh sign-in and synthetic images: authentication, duplicate check, and both the foreground and background upload paths all pass; the HTTP 400 above reproduces only with a deliberately emptied receipt. Why some devices produce an empty receipt is still open — this release makes the queue survive it. - **The Simulator cannot run background uploads or schedule background tasks.** Use a device to exercise real backup behaviour.

Version 0.2 adds a native setup launcher and the first settings pass, plus the controller and New Game renderer fixes. ## What's new - Import your retail PC game folder through Files; check startup files and select Play. - Touch-button and pressed-button opacity sliders. - Controller visibility: Automatic, Always show or Always hide. Hidden controls also stop accepting touch input. - Horizontal/vertical touch-camera sensitivity and invert-Y preference. - Optional compact FPS and average frame-interval display. - Basic logging by default; opt into Detailed for performance samples and bounded traces. - Export a diagnostic report or clear logs with confirmation. - Back up and export existing save slots without replacing the originals. - Settings reset preserves saves, game data and custom button layouts. - App icon for iPhone/iPad. - Includes IndecentDad's physical-controller visibility fix and the MGL texture-deletion fix for the New Game/front-end crash. ## Downloads and installation **Simpsons-Hit-and-Run-iOS-0.2.ipa** is an **unsigned arm64 iPhone/iPad build**, version 0.2 (build 2), targeting iOS 15.0 or later. Sign it with your own Apple account using a compatible sideloading tool. This is not an App Store or universally signed IPA. **No retail game files are included.** This is the **PAL/EFIGS PC-data build**. Import your own compatible installed retail PC game folder using the launcher, or transfer it into Documents/game through Files/Finder. Console ISOs and ZIP import are not supported. Install over the existing app using the same signing identity/bundle identifier to retain its data. Back up your saves first. Deleting the app also deletes its local game data and backups. The inspected IPA contains the executable, dependencies, touch-control artwork, app icon and release documentation. It contains no game_assets folder, retail game archives, save slots or embedded signing profile. - **Source code (zip / tar.gz)**: GitHub's archives for this tag, below. - **Release-Documentation-0.2.zip**: installation, launcher/settings guide, controls, credits and dependency notices; also included in the IPA. - **ffmpeg-6.0.tar.xz**: unmodified source for the statically linked FFmpeg dependency. Build options are in ios-project/build-ffmpeg.sh. - **SHA256SUMS.txt**: checksums for the uploaded packages. See [installation](https://github.com/creeper4004/The-Simpsons-Hit-and-Run-iOS/blob/v0.2/INSTALLATION.md), [settings and save backups](https://github.com/creeper4004/The-Simpsons-Hit-and-Run-iOS/blob/v0.2/ios-project/SETTINGS.md), and [known issues](https://github.com/creeper4004/The-Simpsons-Hit-and-Run-iOS/blob/v0.2/KNOWN_ISSUES.md). ## Validation and limitations Device and simulator Release builds passed. Automated checks cover settings policies, value clamping, frame-rate measurement, diagnostic filtering/clearing, persistent-log concurrency/rotation, startup-file validation and the texture-deletion regression. Simulator UI checks covered settings persistence, diagnostic export, and byte-for-byte save-backup copying with the original retained. The user confirmed FPS display and controller visibility on iPhone 17 Pro Max / iOS 27.2 beta. Prior user retests confirmed game-folder import and that the New Game crash no longer occurred. Broader devices/data editions, longer sessions and full-story completion remain unverified. The FPS display measures game frame submissions and average frame interval, not GPU execution time. Basic versus Detailed logging has not been performance-benchmarked. Save restoration is manual through Files; there is no automatic restore button in this release. **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LinkPass888/AirBeep/compare/v2.5.1...v2.5.2

### English / Changed - **iOS 18 is now supported.** The deployment target drops from iOS 27 to iOS 18.0; the supported range is **iOS/iPadOS 18.0 – 27.2 B2**, and later versions cannot be supported. Below iOS 27 the system does not support on-device pairing — generate a pairing file on a computer with [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) or [idevice_pair](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice_pair) and import it. - **The switch is gone.** The home screen now shows two independent actions: **Silence recording tone**, and either **Back Up Original Tones** (shown until a complete backup exists) or **Restore original tone**. The current tone state is no longer displayed — detecting it needs a device read that is unreliable on some iOS releases. Successful operations confirm with an alert instead. - The home page version line shows the running system version beside the app version, e.g. `iOS 27.1 AirBeep v2.5.1 (9)` (`iPadOS` on iPad). - Backup is a standalone action: back the originals up before silencing so they are always recoverable; the button then flips to Restore. The automatic-backup note sits under that button. ### English / Fixed - **Flaky airlift reads no longer abort the whole operation.** Each tone file is read independently; a failed read is skipped and logged instead of failing the silence/restore. The write channel's return code is the source of truth, and read-back verification degrades to a log entry when a re-read is unavailable. - **Loopback connect no longer falsely demands Wi-Fi.** Wi-Fi presence is now read from the live interface table (`getifaddrs`) instead of `NWPathMonitor`, which reports unsatisfied once the VPN owns the default path. Wi-Fi is still required. - The third writable tone file `StartDisclosure.caf` is now replaced too (skipped automatically on releases that do not ship it). - Restore without a backup explains the language-change recovery path instead of failing with a generic "no backup" error. - Removed the non-public-behavior disclaimer from the bottom of the home page. ### English / Added - **Advanced settings** (About page): set a custom device IP for the loopback connection, and inspect the live network-interface table with tunnel/Wi-Fi state — self-diagnosis for the "connection refused / wrong subnet" reports. - Runtime interface scan: tunnel dials now adapt to the actual network via `al_set_target_hosts` without any route probing. - Localization hardened: two validation scripts keep the EN/zh-Hans catalogs in sync (identical keys, matching placeholders, no untranslated UI literals). --- ### 中文 / 变更 - **支持 iOS 18。** 最低系统要求由 iOS 27 降至 iOS 18.0，支持范围为 **iOS/iPadOS 18.0 – 27.2 B2**，之后的版本无法支持。iOS 27 以下的系统 不支持本机配对，请在电脑上用 [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) 或 [idevice_pair](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice_pair) 生成配对文件后导入。 - **取消开关设计。** 首页改为两个独立操作：**静音录音提示音**，以及 **备份原始提示音**（尚无完整备份时显示）或 **恢复原始提示音**。不再显示 当前提示音状态——检测状态需要在部分 iOS 版本上不可靠的设备读取；操作 成功后以弹窗提示。 - 首页版本行在软件版本号左侧显示当前系统版本，例如 `iOS 27.1 AirBeep v2.5.1 (9)`（iPad 上显示 `iPadOS`）。 - 备份成为独立操作：可先备份再静音，原音始终可找回；按钮随后切换为恢复， 自动备份说明位于该按钮下方。 ### 中文 / 修复 - **airlift 读取偶发失败不再导致整个操作中断。** 每个提示音文件独立读取， 失败仅跳过并记录日志；以写入通道的返回码为准，回读校验在无法读取时 降级为日志记录。 - **回环连接不再误报"需要连接 Wi-Fi"。** Wi-Fi 状态改由实时接口表 （`getifaddrs`）判断，不再使用在 VPN 接管默认路由后总报告不可用的 `NWPathMonitor`。Wi-Fi 仍为必需条件。 - 同时替换第三个可写提示音文件 `StartDisclosure.caf`（未提供该文件的 系统版本自动跳过）。 - 无备份时的恢复会明确指引"更改系统语言"恢复路径，不再报模糊的 "无备份"错误。 - 删除首页底部"依赖非公开系统行为"的免责提示。 ### 中文 / 新增 - **高级设置**（关于页）：可为回环连接设置自定义设备 IP，并查看带 隧道/Wi-Fi 状态的实时网络接口列表，自行排查"连接被拒绝 / 网段不对"问题。 - 运行时接口扫描：通过 `al_set_target_hosts` 让隧道拨号适配实际网络， 不做任何路由探测。 - 本地化加固：新增两个校验脚本保证中英文目录一致（键相同、占位符匹配、 无未翻译界面文案）。 --- **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LinkPass888/AirBeep/compare/v2.4.1...v2.5.1

## [2.4.1] - 2026-10-17 ### English / Fixed - Configure the native Airlift target once from `AIRLIFT_TARGET_HOST` so setup checks and tone operations share the configured LocalDevVPN peer. - Complete the Lockdown heartbeat handshake before accessing network services. Keep the existing heartbeat client alive for each operation and abort its task when the tunnel is dropped, including cached-route connections. - Rebuild the pinned native dependency with the file-read and heartbeat patch; retain checksum and exported-symbol verification. ### 中文 / 修复 - 支持通过构建设置配置 Airlift 连接地址，连接检查与提示音读写共用同一目标。 - 修复网络 Lockdown 路径缺少 heartbeat 导致服务连接被系统关闭的问题；保活仅限本次操作生命周期。 ## What's Changed * Fix Lockdown heartbeat and configurable Airlift target by @kaluli123123 in https://github.com/LinkPass888/AirBeep/pull/22 ## New Contributors * @kaluli123123 made their first contribution in https://github.com/LinkPass888/AirBeep/pull/22 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/LinkPass888/AirBeep/compare/v2.4.0...v2.4.1

# NBA Hangtime 0.4.4 iOS build 9 · Windows x64 · iOS 16 or later ## Changes - Match CRT curvature to the corrected ports: CURVATURE 1.0 with a 40% blend toward the flat image. - Remove frame-artwork overscan and prevent outermost pixels from smearing beyond the curved screen. - Fade the tube boundary into black with a 1.5-pixel edge mask. - Generate the iOS and Windows CRT shaders from the same math. ## Downloads - `NBA-Hangtime-iOS.ipa` — unsigned; sign with your sideloading tool. - `NBA-Hangtime-Windows-x64.zip` - `NBA-Hangtime-0.4.4-source.zip` — matching port and patched core source. Companion SHA-256 checksums are included. Game ROMs are not included; the complete L1.1 arcade set is required. See `SOURCE.md` for source and license notices. ## Validation Geometry regression checks cover the curvature values, symmetry, all four borders and edge fade. Windows and iOS release builds passed. OpenGL and Metal GPU tests passed shader compilation, rendering passes, black corners, image orientation, toggles and resizing. Package integrity and privacy checks passed before publication. GPU tests ran on the Mac host. Visual confirmation on physical iOS and Windows devices remains pending.

# NBA Hangtime 0.4.3 iOS build 8 · Windows x64 · iOS 16 or later ## New in 0.4.3 - Add the NewPixie CRT filter on iOS and Windows. Enable or disable CRT FILTER from the iOS Display menu or Windows pause menu. - Save the setting across launches; default to OFF. Apply changes immediately without restarting the game. - Preserve the original pixel display with CRT off, and reset feedback when toggling or switching widescreen frame sizes. ## Changes since 0.4.0 - Fix Windows Xbox input by reading buttons, sticks and triggers through XInput. Gameplay, controller setup and menus use the same polled input state. - Improve iOS controller event delivery, including Menu/Start and gamepad routing on iOS 18 and later. - Keep controller slots stable across reordering and disconnects. Controllers join as Player 1, Player 3, Player 2 and Player 4. - Align Player 1 and Player 4 possession indicators and scoring flashes with their status plates. - Restore camera tracking at both near-side corners. Limit the inbound view separately so it stays inside the available scenery at both court ends. - Preserve live settings changes, including switching head size during gameplay. Normal, big and huge head settings apply to all four players. - Strip private build paths and debug metadata from release binaries. Check packages for ROMs, signing credentials and development artifacts. - Include license notices and matching source references in both binary packages. ## Downloads - `NBA-Hangtime-Windows-x64.zip` - `NBA-Hangtime-iOS.ipa` (unsigned; sign using your sideloading tool) - `NBA-Hangtime-0.4.3-source.zip` Each archive has a companion SHA-256 checksum. Game ROMs are not included; the complete arcade L1.1 set is required. See `SOURCE.md` for source and distribution notices. ## Validation Windows and iOS release builds succeeded. ROM importer, controller routing, native XInput decoding, controller remapping, camera bounds, live widescreen switching, core bridge and release hygiene tests passed. Physical Xbox testing, visual confirmation of the revised inbound view and GPU rendering of the CRT effect remain unverified on Windows and iOS. The local build environment has no GPU/display access, so the graphics test harnesses could compile but could not run. If CRT is unavailable, the normal picture remains available.

# Changelog v0.4.2 - Updated Xbox controller input on Windows and controller event handling on iOS. - Improved controller setup, remapping, menu navigation, and reconnect handling. - Kept player assignments stable in **P1 → P3 → P2 → P4** order. - Fixed Player 1 and Player 4 possession indicator alignment. - Improved camera tracking so players remain visible at the court corners. - Adjusted the inbound camera at both ends to avoid exposing missing scenery. - Removed private build paths and debug metadata from release binaries. - Added license notices, release notes, and matching source code packaging.

> [!NOTE] > Starting from version 2.0.0, we no longer provide builds of TrollStore JIT. You can package it yourself by following the [guide](https://github.com/Rednick16/TrollStoreJITEnabler). This is a major release focused on a redesigned interface, expanded platform support, and advanced features. Landscape browsing, library management, and external controller navigation have been rebuilt. It also adds several new systems and brings Netplay to eligible Libretro cores. ### Before You Update - Dreamcast (Flycast): Existing save states will no longer work as of 2.0.0. Convert important save states to in-game saves before updating, or back up the `Flycast/dc` folder yourself. - Wii: A BootMii-format `keys.bin` is required. - Symbian: Install firmware in Settings first (`.ROM`; S60v2 and later also need `.RPKG`). - GameCube / Wii: The core is still being optimized, so heat and frame drops should still be expected. - MAME: A number of lesser-used arcade systems have been trimmed. Some obscure titles may no longer run. ### Interface Landscape - A new landscape library, with most landscape pages redesigned. - Built-in dynamic backgrounds. You can use or upload ShaderToy (GLSL) scripts to customize them. Only single-Image scripts are supported; complex scripts may increase battery use or heat. - Multiple customizable card carousel styles. - Focused background: when a game is selected, its banner can be used as the landscape focus backdrop. - background music feature in landscape mode—besides built-in tracks, you can upload your own music files to use as background music. - built in 12 sets of navigation and focus sound effects. Game Options and Shortcuts - A unified options list and interaction model throughout the app. - Available actions are automatically arranged and regrouped for the current context. - Advanced reordering: customize the order and grouping of options. - A redesigned in-game shortcut menu. Shortcuts can appear on supported skins and in the in-game menu. Navigation and Input - A global focus and navigation system for iPhone and iPad. The original Theft4 icon is back. ## What changed - Faster cold geometry conversion and reusable immutable upload backing. - Less work per draw through cached shader metadata, pooled bindings and reusable frame bookkeeping. - Warm pipeline recipes survive cache pressure instead of being cleared together. - Upload VM allocation runs outside the cache mutex; retired sources are cleaned up incrementally and in-flight GPU resources retain their data. - Less CPU busy polling and allocation in multi-object waits. - Native attachment optimizations reduce proven redundant clear/load/store work while preserving the intended image. - Improved compact iPhone launcher layouts. ## Optional Mods menu - **Native Aspect Ratio:** expand the viewport to the launch-window shape, with matching camera/lighting reconstruction, odd-size effects fixes and proportional pause-menu/radar corrections. Updating in place retains existing caches. ## Validation and current limits 33 native contracts, 9 mod contracts and 45 real-Metal graphics cases pass, alongside CPU wait sanitizer checks and Release optimization verification. The target remains under 30 ms of total frame work. Remaining first-use spikes, heavy views and device-specific performance are still being improved; this is not a universal locked-30-FPS guarantee. Host fixture savings are not whole-game FPS percentages. Optional mod coverage still needs broader gameplay testing. # Theft4 0.3 — direct Metal and a rebuilt rendering path Apple version **0.3.0**, build **123**, launcher label **0.3**. Source and the full engineering record are published on GitHub main. The [0.3 GitHub release](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/releases/tag/v0.3) includes the unsigned ARM64 IPA and its checksum. TestFlight publication is separate. The full engineering changelog is [recorded here](https://github.com/KoreanSeats1/Theft4/blob/v0.3/CHANGELOG.md#03--direct-metal-rebuilt-geometry-and-a-faster-native-rendering-path--2026-10-06). 0.3 is the largest rendering change in Theft4 so far. The running game now sends its prepared frames directly to Metal. This includes the actual city, characters, lighting, effects and presentation, rather than just the separate Metal Lab. The renderer and its CPU preparation, resource lifetimes and upload caches have been substantially rebuilt around Apple's graphics API. On the M5 iPad, the tester reports a huge improvement and very good gameplay at the selected native resolution, with a remaining spike that now recovers. Subsequent build 122 testing was also reported as excellent. The latest retrieved native log confirms a 2416×1359 internal/output target with no upscaling. This is much closer to the desired console experience. It does not establish a locked 30 FPS in every scene, uninterrupted long-session stability, or equivalent performance on other hardware. The engineering target remains under 30 ms of frame work, leaving margin inside the 33.3 ms interval for 30 FPS. ## The direct Metal change The previous production rendering route used the GTA IV frontend, Vulkan and MoltenVK before reaching Metal. 0.3 introduces a live Metal worker, native render passes, native resource bindings, completion-owned frame storage and direct CAMetalLayer presentation. Normal Metal gameplay does not realize its draws through the Vulkan provider or presenter. Game shaders are prepared offline from the project's stock shader corpus. Their constant banks and reflected texture/sampler fetches become explicit Metal bindings. The game no longer needs to compile that corpus through a live Vulkan translation path to produce its Metal draws. Pipeline variants and Metal driver compilation can still require work when a new scene is encountered. The game remains an ahead-of-time recompilation of the supported Xbox 360 release. Its compiled ARM64 code still uses the compatibility runtime for the title's memory, service and calling conventions. This release does not replace all game logic with handwritten native code, rewrite physics or traffic, or turn the project into a PC source port. Legacy Vulkan code and libraries remain in the build for comparison and compatibility; direct rendering is a runtime route, not a claim that the application has no Vulkan symbols or dependencies. ## Rendering correctness and clarity - Complete ordered frames now include the game's render passes, color resolves, depth handoffs, reflections and host effects. Draw order and required prior attachment contents are preserved across internal submissions. - The port handles reversed viewport depth, the negative-one-to-one vertex depth convention, attachmentless draws, depth-only pipelines, per-instance stream 16, buffered/indexed rectangles and rotating output drawables. - Packed lighting aliases and the title's float-pair multiple render targets retain their intended channel masks and storage roles. GPU-produced surfaces are distinct from immutable uploaded textures. - Sampling preserves mip ranges, row/plane pitches, layers, cube faces and channel swizzles. Reflection updates wait for valid written content rather than making an entire otherwise valid scene fail. - Blending, alpha discard, sample coverage, output scaling and clamping are checked against the game shader contract. Normal presentation uses GPU textures directly. - Color targets use render-appropriate private storage without unnecessary usage flags that defeated compr

Queue ownership remains ordered, while producer lock contention and worker batch-transfer time were reduced in measured M5 iPad captures. - Common state commands use compact packets, and successfully queued identical bindings can be suppressed. Draws still capture and protect their resource generations. Bounded packet storage reuse reduces construction and release churn across dense scenes. - Immutable vertex-layout requirements and unchanged vertex/index bindings are reused. Validated parent constant blocks receive only changed ranges when an exact fenced frame allocation is available. - Texture content identity is separated from sampler settings. A19 devices walk the texture stages actually used by the shader in selected CPU paths. The existing full traversal remains available as a diagnostic fallback. - Pipeline prewarming is bounded, with A19 prewarm disabled to avoid speculative backlog. A draw whose new pipeline is still compiling can be deferred rather than blocking the entire render worker; check visual correctness when moving into new areas. - Two completion-owned native frame slots preserve overlap without releasing buffers or textures still in flight. The launcher now exposes 540p through 1080p internal resolutions, FSR, graphics quality choices and a performance preset. A19 final output is capped at 1080p to reduce drawable pixel work. - The frame-time graph shows publication intervals and recent spikes. Mean renderer interval changed from 40.57 to 37.84 ms, p95 from 47.58 to 45.58 ms, and frames above 40 ms from 357/599 to 182/599. The routes and GPU work differed, so the whole-frame difference is not a controlled proof of a fixed percentage FPS uplift. See the [capture review](lab-experiments/build33-device-review.md). Heavy scenes and thermal state still matter. An A19 iPhone Air capture in serious thermal state had a 44.5 ms median renderer interval; another run in different conditions was 33.2 ms. Scene and output size differed, and the captures do not measure CPU clocks or device power. Lower resolution and the 1080p output cap can reduce pixel workload, but lower heat and battery use still require controlled device measurement. apps.localizedDescription: A static recompilation of Skate 3 for iOS, rendering through Vulkan on MoltenVK. Runs at a locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini (A15): median frame 16.7ms, 95th percentile 16.8-17.8ms. YOU MUST SUPPLY THE GAME. This app contains no game content and will not start without it. AFTER INSTALLING: 1. Connect your iPhone to a computer and open Finder > your iPhone > Files > Skate 3 (on Windows, iTunes > File Sharing). 2. Drop in a 'game' folder containing your own disc files. That is about 6GB, so allow a few minutes. 3. Add Title Update 3, the free update EA published on Xbox Live - it is not on the disc and the game will not run without it. The app can download it for you: choose "Install the title update" and then Download. If you would rather supply it yourself, copy the package into the same Skate 3 folder and it is found automatically. The setup screens walk you through steps 2 and 3. On-screen touch controls appear when no controller is attached; MFi and Bluetooth controllers are picked up automatically. Press Start + Select together for a performance menu that shows your frame rate and what is limiting it. Requires iOS 16.0 or later.

versions.localizedDescription: # Skate 3 Recompiled v2.7.1 — iOS iOS skipped a release. Everything Android got in v0.2.0 is here, plus two iOS-specific defaults. 24 engine commits and 17 SDK commits since v2.6.3. ## Put any button anywhere Full controller remapping, on the Controls page under **Button Mapping**. Sixteen inputs — the four face buttons, both bumpers, both triggers, both stick clicks, Back, Start and the four D-pad directions — can each be moved to any of the others. Your mapping is saved and survives an update. The sticks themselves are not remapped; Swap Sticks and Invert Camera Y already cover that. ## Three bugs that were costing you frames **Touching the frame-rate row uncapped the game.** One setting's name was a prefix of another's (`..._fps_cap` inside `..._fps_cap_auto`), so changing the Framerate Cap row erased the shipped cap entirely, on every launch after you touched that row. The game then ran the guest loop uncapped. On Android that also meant rendering roughly twice the frames the panel could show and dumping the rest as heat, which is what "runs at 60, drops after a few minutes" was there; iOS presents through FIFO, so the cost here is wasted work rather than heat. **"The frame rate is fine but it feels like slow motion."** Skate 3 advances exactly one refresh period of simulation per rendered frame, however long that frame took, so a 33 ms frame runs the game at half speed. The ceiling that lets a frame advance more than one period (skate3_frame_advance_cap) had been compiled for Switch only — iOS and Android, the two platforms whose frames overrun the period most, never got it. It is compiled in on iOS now. Being straight about this one: the clamp is in and reachable, but raising it was measured as changing nothing on hardware, so treat it as a lever that now exists rather than a fix you are guaranteed to feel. **A profiler was running in every build.** A per-packet GPU timer took two clock reads and two atomic increments on every command packet — around 1.7 million clock reads a second on the busiest thread — whether or not anyone was profiling. It is off unless you ask for it. ## First launch could come up blank Roughly one clean install in ten reached the setup screen with an empty options list and no way forward. Parts of a screen drawn once while their shaders were still compiling were skipped and never came back — and the difficulty prompt is drawn exactly once. Shader compilation now stays synchronous through the cold-boot frontend, so nothing can draw before it is ready. ## New in Settings Eleven new rows, most of them aimed at buying frames back on a phone: - **3D Scene Resolution** — Full / 75% / 67% / 50% / 40%, separate from UI sharpness - **Draw Distance** — now goes down to Quarter and Eighth - **NPC Update Rate** and **World Update Rate** - **Pedestrians & Traffic**, **Movable Props**, **Other Skaters** — stop the world spawning crowds you are not looking at (all three need a restart) - **Vegetation**, **Hair Detail**, **Water Effects**, **Draw Batching** - **Framerate Cap** — 40, 45 and 50 added (40 divides 120 Hz, 45 divides 90 Hz) - **FPS Percentiles** — the 1% low and p95/p99 next to the average (darchap's, see Credit). Known limitation on the three population cuts: they remove the bodies, not the gameplay objects behind them, so you may still hear pedestrians, traffic and other skaters you cannot see. Being worked on. The average is exactly the statistic that hides a stutter: a steady 60 and a 60 that drops four frames a second read the same. ## Two changed defaults on iOS - **Draw distance now ships at Half.** The static world is roughly 750 of the 765 things drawn in a frame, so it is the only content lever with real weight behind it. The trade is real: props, street furniture and foliage pop in closer than they did in 2.6.3. **Settings > Video > Draw Distance > Original** puts it back. **This applies to new installs only.** If you are updating, your existing draw distance is kept exactly as it is — the

> **Superseded by [v2.7.1](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** > This build shipped the in-app title-update install, which still works exactly as described below. > It also shipped the Framerate Cap row that silently erased the 60 fps cap on every later launch — fixed in 2.7.1. ### Original v2.6.3 notes **The title update can now be installed from inside the app.** Previously iOS could do neither half of this: the "select a file" route went through the system document picker, which does not work under TrollStore or on a jailbreak, and the download button was never shown at all. Players who had just installed from a disc image were left able to install the game and then unable to install the update it requires. Both routes work now: - **Download it in the app.** Tap "Install the title update" and then Download. It fetches the 1.7 MB package and installs it, with no computer involved. - **Or copy it in yourself.** A package already sitting in your Skate 3 folder is found automatically, the same way disc images have been found since 2.6.0. No picker, no file browser. **A home screen on iOS.** The app now opens on a launcher instead of straight into the game: Play, install from a disc image, install the title update, choose a map pack, and save a diagnostic report you can share from the Files app. Every row returns to it, so you can install a disc, then the update, then pick a pack in one sitting. **Settings now stick.** Twenty-four rows were being forced back to their defaults at every launch - resolution, V-Sync, MSAA, shadows, ambient occlusion, bloom, sun shafts, draw distance, the frame cap, and the audio and interface rows. The menu wrote your choice to disk and startup overwrote it on the way back in, so the rows looked broken. Audio Buffer Size in particular simply never applied. Opening and closing the settings menu also used to freeze the per-device memory budgets at whatever that one launch happened to pick; it no longer writes rows you did not touch. **Map pack names in other languages.** A pack built for one market carries English text and leaves the other languages empty, and the game was showing those empty slots - an unnamed entry in the map list and raw identifiers where level names belong, reported as the DLC maps not loading in French or Spanish. Names now fall back to English instead of coming back blank. This is fixed in the game rather than in the packs, so it applies to every pack you already have. Requires iOS 16.0 or later and a 6-core device. You still supply your own copy of the game.

> **Superseded by [v2.6.3](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** This build cannot install Title Update 3 on a TrollStore or jailbreak install: its download button was never shown on iOS, and the file picker it falls back to does not work there. v2.6.3 fixes both. ### Original v2.6.0 notes Skate 3 on iOS, v2.6.0. **You must supply the game.** This app contains no game content. See the [setup instructions](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup#readme). ## The completion-screen slowdown Mission completion and replay screens crawled, and a long session decayed toward single digits and then died with no crash report. Finished graphics work is destroyed a little at a time so no single frame stalls. Past a threshold that limit is supposed to come off entirely and let the backlog clear. The clock came off; a cap of 256 objects per frame did not. Once a screen produced them faster than that, the backlog could only grow, every frame paid to work against a longer one, and the heap grew until iOS killed the app. Measured on an iPhone 13 mini: a backlog of 18,000 falling by exactly 255 a frame for seventy frames at 5-36ms each, and one of those cleanups finishing its 255 objects in **508 microseconds** before stopping anyway. It is now one limit instead of two - a 50ms ceiling with no object cap - so the backlog actually clears. ## Quitting to the home screen after switching away Switching to another app and back could end the game with "Graphics device lost". iOS refuses GPU work to an app in the background, and those refusals keep arriving for a few milliseconds after it returns. They were charged to a budget meant to absorb one occasional error every few seconds: eight arrived inside 20 milliseconds, and the ninth was treated as a real hardware failure. Failures caused by backgrounding are now recognised as such, within a bounded window so a genuinely lost device is still reported rather than hidden behind a frozen screen. ## Installing the game without the file picker Under TrollStore or on a jailbreak, the system file picker cannot hand the app a file, and the picker was the only way to select a disc image. LiveContainer worked only because it ships its own replacement. Drop your disc image into the **Skate 3 folder in Files** and it is found automatically, with no picker involved. Every candidate is verified as a real Xbox 360 disc before it is used. The picker remains available for iCloud Drive and USB storage. An extracted disc copied across as a folder is also accepted now. Previously `default.xex` one level down read as "game files not found". ## Also - Texture and mesh budgets are back to the values 2.5.0 shipped. - The frame-time log names what the cleanup freed and which limit stopped it. - Android build support is in the tree; this release is iOS only. Requires iOS 16 and a 6-core device. Every iPhone that runs iOS 16 qualifies; older iPads (A9/A9X/A10/A10X) do not.

> **Superseded by [v2.6.0](https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest).** > This build slows down on mission completion and replay screens, and a long > session decays toward single-digit frame rates. Use the latest release. ### Original v2.5.0 notes # Skate 3 for iOS — v2.5.0 Hey — this one's a big catch-up. The last public release was **v2.4.0**, and everything from 2.4.1 through 2.4.7 got built and then never actually shipped, so all of it lands here at once along with the new stuff. Install it with AltStore or SideStore. The `.ipa` doesn't contain the game — you bring your own copy of Skate 3 and it walks you through installing it the first time you launch. --- The headline: **the game used to measure itself while you played, and now it doesn't.** Every build up to this point shipped with the performance tools running — a frame-timing summary, a present-cadence tracker, and a ten-clock breakdown of literally every frame that went to the screen. The lines they wrote to the log were cheap. The bookkeeping behind them ran on every single frame whether anything got printed or not, and everybody paid for it just to play the game. That's all off now. It didn't get deleted, though — that detail is what makes a bug report useful. It moved behind a **Diagnostics switch in Settings → System**. If something goes wrong and someone asks you for a log, flip it on, play until it happens again, and send the log. No special build, no config files to hand-edit. **The settings menu asks before it closes the game now.** On iOS, applying a setting that needs a restart means quitting — that's genuinely the only way some of them can take effect — and it used to just do it, instantly, the moment you picked it. Worse, it was also wired to a bare button on a controller, so one stray press and your session was gone. It asks now, and "Keep Playing" is the option your thumb lands on by default. **And the buttons are actually sized for fingers.** Those little circles either side of each setting were built for a mouse pointer. On a phone they worked out to about two millimetres across — roughly a third of what a touch target is supposed to be — and the invisible margin around them didn't scale at all. They are more than twice the size now, with a proper margin, and the rows and category buttons grew to match. **A Potato preset**, under Settings → Video → Preset, sitting below Performance. It gives the picture up rather than trimming it: no shadows at all, no ambient occlusion, bloom or sun shafts, and half the draw distance. For older phones, or for anyone who just wants every frame the hardware can produce. **Half draw distance is selectable now.** The Draw Distance setting used to bottom out at "Original" — it'll go to "Half" now, which draws less of the world than the Xbox 360 itself did. On a phone this is the setting with the most room behind it, because the emulated CPU is what issues all the draw calls, so cutting them lands on emulation rather than on the GPU. **Logs got a lot quieter.** The content scan used to fire off about fifty warnings every boot about files that were completely fine, which buried anything that actually mattered. A log now leads with the build version and reports real problems. --- ### Everything from the releases that never went out **Frame rate** - iPhones with ProMotion displays (13 Pro and newer) were running the entire game at **30 fps**. That's fixed — they run at 60 now. Touching the screen also halved the frame rate on those phones, which is fixed too. - *Every* iPhone was running at **half the frame rate it should have been.** The graphics layer was encoding each frame's work inline while it submitted it, which serialised two things that are supposed to overlap. Measured on a real device: 30 fps to 60. **Freezes and crashes** - The game could go permanently black while the audio just kept playing. One transient graphics error latched a flag that nothing ever cleared, and every frame after that

**config menu, more control options, and setup that explains itself.** Runs at a **locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini** (A15). Median frame 16.7ms against a 16.67ms budget, 95th percentile 16.8–17.8ms. so it is a real 60, not an average with dips hiding inside it. Anything newer than an A15 has more headroom than that. 70 fps uncapped in career mode and 90 fps in custom maps. Press start and select together to get into config menu --- ## Installing **1. Install the app.** Download `skate3.ipa` below and sideload it with [Live Container] [AltStore](https://altstore.io), [SideStore](https://sidestore.io) or [Sideloadly](https://sideloadly.io). Each re-signs it with your own Apple ID as it installs — the file here is deliberately unsigned. On a free Apple ID the app stops opening after 7 days and needs refreshing; a paid developer account lasts a year. **2. Add your own copy of the game.** The app ships with no game content and will not start without it. Connect your iPhone to a computer, open **Finder → your iPhone → Files → Skate 3** (on Windows, iTunes → File Sharing), and drop in a `game` folder containing your disc files. A full disc image is around 6 GB, so give it a few minutes. **3. Add Title Update 3.** The game needs the free update EA published on Xbox Live; it is not on the disc, and the game will not run without it. iOS apps can't download it themselves, so fetch it on a computer: > **[Download Title Update 3](https://xboxunity.net/Resources/Lib/TitleUpdate.php?tuid=21774)** — about 1.7 MB, from the Xbox Unity archive. The file is named `TU_12K2276_000000C000000.00000000000O3`. Copy it into **Files → On My iPhone → Skate 3**, the same way you staged the disc, then point the installer at it. It is checked against a known SHA-256 before use, so a truncated download is caught immediately rather than crashing later. Setup now walks you through steps 2 and 3 on-screen, and no longer offers a Download button on iOS that could never have worked. That was the part nobody could get past: a 6 GB disc image cannot be picked out of the Files app if it was never copied to the phone in the first place, and the old screen just said "Select ISO" without saying how. Requires iOS 16.0 or later. Controllers pair automatically; touch controls appear when none is attached. --- ## New in this release **Press Start + Select together to open the performance menu.** It shows what the game is actually doing — frame rate, frame time, how long each frame spends waiting on the GPU — and then says in one line what is holding it back: the frame cap, the graphics card, or the emulation itself. That last line is the useful one. Turning quality settings down only buys you frames while it says the graphics card; if it says emulation, you are switching things off for nothing. Every quality setting worth changing sits on the same page under the readout, so you can change one and watch the number move. **More control options.** Vibration strength, so you can soften the constant road buzz without losing the bails. Stick and trigger deadzones, for a worn controller that drifts on its own. Invert camera Y, and swap sticks. Each of the three shortcuts — settings, performance, level picker — can be rebound. Everything defaults to exactly what the console did, so if you change nothing, nothing changes. --- This contains no game content, and never downloads any. You supply your own copy.

# ⚠️ There is a newer version **Download v2.4.0 instead → https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest** v2.3.0 already runs at a locked 60fps; v2.4.0 keeps that and adds a performance menu on Start + Select, more controller options, and setup that explains how to get the game onto your phone. If you use AltStore or SideStore, you don't need to download anything by hand — add this source and it will keep itself updated: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/master/source.json ``` --- ### Original 2.3.0 notes **Locked 60fps.** Previous builds ran 45-50fps in career mode and drifted down over a session. This one holds a locked 60 on an iPhone 13 mini — median frame 16.7ms, and the 95th percentile is 16.8-17.8ms, so it's not an average with dips hiding in it. **Occlusion culling now works on iOS.** It never had. The depth grid it needs was only ever produced inside the ambient-occlusion pass, which iOS switches off to save memory — so the feature was silently doing nothing since the port began. It now builds that grid in a pass of its own. Roughly 480,000 hidden items are culled per session instead of zero. **The emulated passes the native renderer replaces are now skipped.** GPU timing showed the leftover emulation plumbing cost more per frame than drawing the actual world — 10 render-pass entries alone were 3.2ms, and on a phone GPU every one of those is a full tile load/store. Removing them took GPU time from 17.8-19.4ms to 11.0-11.9ms against a 16.67ms budget. **The world is drawn at console distance again.** Draw and LOD distance had been defaulting to twice what the Xbox 360 used, which is roughly four times the world area streaming — affordable standing still, not affordable at speed. That was behind the slowdowns when you built up speed through an area. **The startup and resume hangs are fixed.** Both were the same bug: the renderer allowed as many frames in flight as the swapchain had images, so it could ask for a drawable while every one was still held, and wait forever. There is now always one spare. Also: the texture cache budgets are bounded properly, which keeps memory near 1GB instead of 1.4GB and stops the frame-time drift over long sessions; caches are handed back when the app is backgrounded so iOS is less likely to evict it; and a logging bug is fixed that could turn a recoverable guest fault into a hang. **If lighting looks wrong** in some areas, add `native_render_suppress_mode=2` to `Documents/user/ios_args.txt` — that trades a few fps for the old behavior. As always: this contains no game content. You supply your own copy of the game.

# ⚠️ There is a newer version **Download v2.4.0 instead → https://github.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/releases/latest** This build (2.1.2) predates the 60fps work. v2.4.0 holds a locked 60fps on an iPhone 13 mini - median frame 16.7ms, 95th percentile 16.8-17.8ms. If you use AltStore or SideStore, you don't need to download anything by hand — add this source and it will keep itself updated: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/master/source.json ``` --- ### Original 2.1.2 notes The crash that kept ending sessions is fixed, at full frame rate. **You supply the game.** This release contains no game content. After installing, copy your own extracted game data into Files → On My iPhone → Skate 3 → game, and Title Update 3 alongside it. ## Fixed A fault inside MoltenVK's presentation path had been ending sessions at unpredictable times. It survived every fix aimed at memory, swapchain lifetime and the system's low-memory warning, and MoltenVK's latest release still has it. Presenting through a command buffer rather than calling presentDrawable directly builds the completion handler elsewhere and does not fault. The other workaround — synchronous submits — also worked but halved the frame rate, so this is the one that ships. Also in this release: the hang from moving quickly through the start menus, and a swapchain that could be destroyed while Metal still had work queued against it. ## Install Add this source in AltStore or SideStore: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/andrewnakas/skate3-ios-setup/master/source.json ``` Or download the .ipa below and sideload it. It is unsigned — you sign it with your own Apple ID. A free Apple ID works. ## Custom maps Drop a pack folder (its `.big` and `.header` together) at the top of the app's Documents folder. # MeleePad 0.2.5 Fixes iPhone and iPad imports that could report success after a game resource was only partially written, for example when storage ran out. Import now checks each extracted file against the disc's expected length before activating the new data. An incomplete extraction shows an error and leaves the previous installation and saves in place so you can free space and try again. Use PadMint to build the updated app from your own supported Melee disc. Install over your existing copy with the same signing identity to preserve its data. This release contains the unsigned app shell without game code, the PadMint recipe, and checksums. PadMint builds your game module locally; keep the resulting personal IPA private. The regression runs the app's actual extraction wrapper with a synthetic DiscIO boundary. It covers complete output, a truncated final file with the same file count, missing files, a directory in place of a file, and nested/empty files under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The unmodified wrapper fails the truncated-file case. This establishes the extraction repair, not physical-device or provider-specific picker acceptance, gameplay, audio, or performance.

# Playport 0.4.0: GOG, Epic Games and your own games **Playport is no longer only for Steam.** Sign in to **GOG** or **Epic Games** and install your games from there, or bring any DRM-free PC game from Files. Games now sign in to their store as they would on a PC. ## Highlights ### 🛒 GOG and Epic Games In **Settings › Accounts**, next to Steam, you can now sign in to **GOG** and **Epic Games** (the setup checklist's Accounts step offers all three). Your Windows games from each store show up in the Library, with their own filter and the store's artwork. - **Install, Update, Verify and Repair** work just as they do for Steam, through the same Downloads queue. When a store has a newer build, the game's page shows **Update**. - If Epic's sign-in asks you to do something first, such as accept an updated privacy policy, the sign-in sheet tells you what. Do that on Epic's site, then press Try again. - Games that use anti-cheat or another company's launcher are refused before the install, and their page says why. ### 🔑 Games sign in to their store A game now gets what its store's launcher would give it, with nothing to set up: - **Epic:** every Epic game starts signed in to your Epic account, including games that check you own them. Games using Epic Online Services sign in too: Snakebird Complete reaches its menu signed in. - **Steam:** games get the tickets Steam gives them on a PC, so online sign-ins through Steam work. Valheim logs in to its online service this way. - **GOG:** games built with GOG Galaxy sign in to it. Moonscars signs in. - **Sign-in pages in a panel.** When a game opens a web page, such as Epic's "Allow" page the first time an online game signs in, it appears in a panel over the game; close it to go back to the game. ### 📁 Add a game from Files Have a DRM-free PC game already? Press **X** in the Library, or choose **Add a game**, and pick its folder or a `.zip` from Files. Playport copies it into its own drive and adds it to your Library under **Local**. Pick the game's `.exe` on its page if Playport doesn't find it. Installers (`setup.exe`) are not run: pick the installed game's folder instead. For GOG games, use the GOG account. It needs no installer. ### 🚪 Death's Door runs on Some Unity games, such as Death's Door, quit after about 14 seconds because Windows ran out of address space for them. Playport now places those allocations where there is room, and Death's Door plays into the game. ## Also new - **iOS 26.0 fix:** 0.3.3 closed at launch on iOS 26.0.x. # Playport 0.3.3: JIT your way **Playport now works with the JIT tools you already use.** Its built-in JIT helper is still the easiest way to play. But if you already enable JIT with **StikDebug**, or run your apps inside **LiveContainer**, Playport now takes JIT from them too. You no longer need Playport's own pairing. ## Highlights ### 🔌 Choose where JIT comes from A new **JIT method** setting in **Settings › Setup check** (or press **X** on the setup checklist's first step) offers three ways: | Method | What happens when you press Play | | --- | --- | | **Built-in** (default) | Playport's own helper enables JIT, as before. No other app, no app switch. | | **StikDebug** | Playport opens StikDebug, which enables JIT and brings you back to the game. | | **Another app** | Playport waits for JIT from the app you use, such as LiveContainer's *Launch with JIT*. | StikDebug and other apps use StikDebug's standard **`universal.js`** script. Playport's JIT already speaks its protocol, so there is no custom script to install. ### 📦 LiveContainer support LiveContainer can't start Playport's built-in helper, so Playport now notices when it runs inside LiveContainer and hides the Built-in method. Two ways to play: 1. **Launch with JIT** (recommended): in LiveContainer, set the JIT enabler to StikDebug with `universal.js`, and turn on *Launch with JIT* for Playport. Playport finds JIT already there, so Play doesn't wait for it. 2. **StikDebug from Playport**: choose StikDebug as the JIT method and turn on *Use LiveContainer's Bundle ID* in LiveContainer's settings. ### 🧭 A setup that fits your method - With StikDebug or another app, Playport's own **pairing is no longer a setup step**, and a missing pairing never stops a game. - LocalDevVPN is skipped too when another app brings JIT. StikDebug still uses it. - While a game waits for JIT, the launch screen says what it is waiting for. If JIT doesn't arrive, it tells you what to check for the method you chose. ## Good to know - **One game per launch.** After a game, Playport normally restarts itself so the next one gets fresh JIT. That restart needs Playport's pairing, and inside LiveContainer it isn't possible at all. In those cases Playport asks you to close it and launch it again (with JIT) before the next game. - **Built-in is unchanged** and still the default. If it works for you, there is nothing to do. - **Not tested with StikDebug or LiveContainer yet.** Playport is tested on one phone (iOS 27.0), which has neither. Built-in was checked with Hollow Knight. If you play through StikDebug or LiveContainer, please tell us how it goes. Thanks to the player who asked for this: *"in app JIT enabling is cool and all, but it doesn't work under LiveContainer"*. Now it should: let us know. Everything else is as in 0.3.2.

# Playport 0.3.1: pairing code fix A small fix to 0.3.0's first-time setup. ## Fixes - The pairing code in "Set up game debugging" now shows as plain text in the setup screen. # Playport 0.3.0: 32-bit games **32-bit Windows games now run on your iPhone.** Until now Playport ran only 64-bit games. 0.3.0 adds a full 32-bit runtime with Direct3D 9 graphics on Apple's GPU, and **Portal 2** is the first 32-bit game that plays: menus, test chambers, both portals, sound, controller, saves and Steam Cloud. Everything runs locally on a non-jailbroken iPhone: no streaming, no remake, no PC. ## Highlights ### 🧩 32-bit Windows games - 32-bit (x86) games run next to 64-bit ones, from the same Library and the same Play button. Nothing to set up. - iOS keeps the lowest 4 GB of memory to itself, which is exactly where a 32-bit game has to live. Playport gives each 32-bit game its own 4 GB window higher up and translates every memory access on the fly, so the game never notices. ### 🎨 Direct3D 9 on the iPhone's GPU, through KosmicKrisp - Direct3D 9 runs on DXVK, then Vulkan, then Metal through **KosmicKrisp**, Mesa's Vulkan driver for Apple GPUs, ported to iOS for Playport. - 32-bit games pick Vulkan automatically. Game options show "Default · Vulkan". - KosmicKrisp keeps its compiled shaders on disk, so the second launch of a game reuses them instead of compiling again. ### 🌀 Portal 2 - Plays at **about 60 FPS at 720p**. A 5-minute play with portals, tunnels, a death and a reload averaged 58.4 FPS. - A 95-minute session with saving and loading ran without a crash. After a long session the phone gets warm, and Portal 2 then runs at about 50 FPS. - Saves sync with Steam Cloud, so you can carry on where you left off on your PC. ### ⚡ Faster 32-bit games - x87 floating-point math, which older 32-bit games use heavily, now runs at the CPU's native 64-bit precision, as Valve's Proton does on ARM64. Portal 2's main thread does about 40 % less work and the CPU draws about 40 % less power, so the phone stays cooler and holds 60 FPS for longer. ## Fixes and improvements - Controllers work in games that bring their own copy of XInput (Portal 2 does). - Steam Cloud: Portal 2's saves upload again, and a file Steam refuses no longer stops the whole sync. - Games that ask for Tahoma show their text: Playport now ships fallback Tahoma fonts. - A new opening animation while your stores load, and a launch that dives into the game's art. The game then fades in at its own size. - A game's art fills the screen on its page and during its launch. ## Known limitations - Portal 2 is the only 32-bit game tested so far. Other 32-bit Direct3D 9 games use the same route, but expect rough edges. Please tell us how they run. - 32-bit games run only on Vulkan. Choosing DXMT for one, on its page or globally, stops it from starting. - Expect short hitches when a level loads and the first time you see a new effect. - In long sessions the iPhone heats up and lowers its clock speeds, and frame rates drop. ## Install Download `Playport-0.3.0.ipa` and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version, install over it: your games, saves and Steam login stay. Bring your own games from Steam.
